newsitem.title: UK: Bear markets in base metals nearly over - Waterside.
newsitem.headline: Bear markets in base metals nearly over - Waterside.

text.p: The bear markets in base metals are nearly over and most prices will not collapse under the 1993 lows before bottoming out, Waterside Futures Ltd said.

Copper and aluminium should retest the lows and bounce while only zinc and tin are likely to breach the three-year nadir, with zinc diving as far as $513 and tin as low as $3,608, it said in its latest report.

"There is good reason to believe that most base metals will not break the 1993 lows -- the bear market is already in a mature stage...," said Waterside, which used Elliot Wave technical analysis in the report.
The US stock market is approaching a major peak, which is expected to be followed by a long-term bear market of proportions not experienced since 1929, it said.
This could pressure base metal prices immediately following a crash, but the metals market should reverse and move higher much before share prices do so, as they did in the 1930s.
"It can be seen from the long-term charts that metals will gain favour long before stocks eventually bottom out," it said.
Copper's recent spike higher above $2,000 has peaked and will lead to a slump to the lows of 1993.
"Viewing the pattern from the post-Sumitomo lows at $1,745, we can see the following advance terminate at $2,160," it said.
"This advance was a classic counter-trend pattern, confirming that prices will eventually break below $1,745 and head toward $1,612," the report added.
Aluminium's bull market ended in 1988 at $3,266, followed by a 68-percent decline to $1,037 in October 1993.
But the five-year time span was much too short to fully correct the long-term bull market that had lasted 49 years.
Prices are expected to move towards the $1,037 level in the medium term, but find strong support there.
"If the next declines equal the first, then the ultimate targets can ge verified towards $1,049 sometime next year," the report said.
"However, wave patterns indicate an interim advance is soon to begin from the current lows, with maximum targets towards $1,547 before the last sequence of declines begin to unfold."
In zinc, a long-term bull market topped at $2,000 per tonne in 1989 and the resulting bear market is much different than the other metals.
"Whereas most others are unlikely to exceed the 1993 lows, zinc is almost certainly destined to break below it," Waterside said.
This scenario is based on a descending triangle that targets ultimate lows around $513-$521, "but it will be some time before this selling emerges", it added.
In the short term, an advance should be seen towards $1,096 before the fresh lows are carved out.
The tin market, after having seen a 1989 high, is showing a pattern similar to most of the other metals.
"Three wave declines and advances have formed, suggesting that will take several years to complete. The downside target for the correction is towards $3,608 to $3,859 level," it said.
Lead prices are expected to accelerate lower, moving into a long-term triangle with converging border lines.
"From this we can forecast that declines are already beginning from this year's high at $863 and are targeted next year towards minimum $514," it said.
Nickel has been in a long-term corrective process since surging to a $18,750 high touched in 1989, but it will take several years for this to complete.
Within a triangle pattern, prices are expected to surge towards $13,000 next year once the correction from $10,525 hit in 1995 is completed.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8065
